result.strongest_objection: The design's compatibility path rests on an unverified caller inventory. §3.2 justifies keeping New(ctx, cfg) 'for its 47 test call sites' — a specific, countable codebase claim with no banked verification row (V1 P1–P14 contain greps for far weaker claims, including a 0-match doctor grep with a positive control, but no census of New's callers) — and the load-bearing implicit premise that New's only non-test caller is Run via startBounded is likewise asserted, never verified. If any other production caller of daemon.New exists (any subcommand, tool, or test helper in another package that constructs a real daemon), it silently gains a fresh min(caller-deadline, 9s) registry clock with changed failure timing, §4's Claim A proof ('Run calls startDaemon…') does not cover it, and §9's conflict-surface table is missing an affected caller — a simultaneous hit on gate 1 (unverified premise) and gate 2 (incomplete conflict surface).
result.catch: The shipped operator strings assert an unmeasured cause. §3.4 and V10 tell the operator the profile was left out because 'the host was too busy' and the fix is 'restart when the host is quieter', but out_of_time proves only that the startup clock ran out before any arm was judged; the doc's own §3.2 and R2 name non-load causes that produce the identical flag (a cold binary archive after a pin change, an oversized srt tree, a slow pre-probe step), and the load attribution of the original incident is claim 6, which the doc itself marks 'Not re-measured'. The prescription survives, but the diagnosis is baked into log, health-advice, and doctor text as fact. (Also unbanked: commitBudget '3 s (B6)', the HealthResponse additive requirement at daemon.go:610, the doctor line's 240-byte cap, and -race while the patch introduces mutable package vars as test seams.)
result.proposed_fix:
Add a verification-log row (e.g. V19) and amend the proofs to use it: bank `grep -rn 'daemon\.New(\|= New(\|[^A-Za-z_.]New(' host cmd --include='*.go'` split into test and non-test callers, observed as '47 call sites in *_test.go; sole non-test caller daemon.go:1284 startBounded→Run'; open Claim A's proof with 'New's callers are Run via startBounded and tests only (V19)' and add a compat-path row to §9's conflict table naming the non-test-caller guard (e.g., a small test or vet rule asserting no production caller of New outside daemon.Run, so a future caller cannot silently inherit the fresh clock). Separately, reword the §3.4 log line and the V10 doctor text to claim only what the flag proves: 'exec profile "

": its startup probe was still unfinished when the startup clock ran out (every failed arm was judged after the deadline); see the startup log for what preceded the probe — host load, a cold binary archive, or a slow pre-probe step; restart serve once that clears' — replacing the asserted 'host load' cause. Finally, run the six new tests once under -race and record it, since startupBudget/registryPhaseBudget become mutable package vars used as test seams.

result.strongest_objection: §4 Claim D is stated as a universal ('out_of_time never names an in-time refusal as load') that the mechanism does not establish and that the doc's own §3.3 contradicts. `fail` marks an arm `spent` by one test only: judged at-or-after the startup-clock deadline (exec_probe.go:447). A probe run that starts with milliseconds of clock left can have every arm refuse genuinely (the pass-through shim in T2's control row produces exactly such real refusals) yet have every `fail` call land after the deadline, making all arms `spent` and `OutOfTime()` true — an in-time refusal named as load. The proof offered ('returns false as soon as one failed arm is not spent') establishes only the weaker converse ('any arm judged in time ⇒ out_of_time false'), not the claim. Two compounding claims are also wrong or unverified: §3.3's 'conservative in one direction: when in doubt, it says "an arm refused"' is false — errors exist in both directions (this post-deadline-refusal window mislabels refusal as load; R3's per-run-8s case mislabels load as refusal) — and the asserted 'few milliseconds' window bound has no verification-log entry measuring it. Impact is bounded (advice text only; the profile is still excluded, Claim C intact), but a by-construction argument containing a disproven universal is precisely what this quorum tier exists to catch.
result.catch: Fix the §3.3/§4 overclaim and expose the gap with a test. Specifically: the truth table in T4 has no row for 'genuine refusal judged after the deadline' — add it; under the current code it returns OutOfTime()==true, contradicting Claim D as written. Then either (a) restate Claim D as the one-directional bound the proof actually gives, delete the 'never' and the 'conservative in one direction' sentences, and move the residual window into §6 with a measured bound (a new verification-log entry timing worst-case arm-judgment latency relative to the deadline), or (b) change the `spent` rule from judgment wall-time to a cause-based test (arm failure is context.DeadlineExceeded or the budget-spent sentinel), which makes the universal claim genuinely true by construction — but note this flips R3's classification, so R3 and T4's rows must be re-derived. Separately verify that M1's `git apply` step includes the new-file presence guard added in the V17 script after the vacuous-apply incident; the milestone as written reproduces exactly the failure signature V17 discarded (rc 0, no output, patch possibly skipped).
result.proposed_fix: Replace §4 Claim D with: 'Claim D (one-directional bound on the load label). OutOfTime() returns false as soon as one failed arm is not spent, and false when nothing failed; therefore out_of_time=true certifies only that every failed arm was judged at-or-after the probe deadline. Two residual mislabels remain, both advice-only because applyProbe deletes the profile regardless (Claim C): (i) a genuine refusal judged after the deadline — reachable only by a run that began inside the judgment-latency window of the deadline; measured bound in V19 (<=N ms on this rig, derived from the arm-judgment timestamps banked at $V/designer-judgment-latency.txt); (ii) a per-run 8s timeout with startup time remaining is labeled an arm failure (R3). The classification therefore errs toward investigation in case (ii) and toward a restart hint in case (i); neither direction serves the profile.' Update §3.3's bullet to match (delete 'conservative in one direction'), add the T4 row 'all arms refuse genuinely, judgments land after the deadline ⇒ OutOfTime true, profile still excluded and never served' asserting Claim C rather than the false universal, add §6 R9 recording the (i) window and its measured bound, and amend M1's apply step to: `git apply --check design_docs/planned/w-daemon-startup-under-load.patch && git apply design_docs/planned/w-daemon-startup-under-load.patch && test -f host/daemon/startup_under_load_test.go && test -f host/broker/exec_probe_out_of_time_test.go && test -f cmd/ailang-worldd/doctor_exec_profiles_test.go` with the note that V17 showed `git apply` can return rc 0 while skipping every path when run from a subdirectory of an enclosing repo.

result.strongest_objection: The new diagnostic asserts a cause that its implementation does not establish. Marking failures by when fail() observes them proves neither that startup timeout caused the failures nor that host load caused the timeout. Nevertheless, doctor says 'the host was too busy' and 'nothing to fix in the profile.' A genuine probe refusal can be observed after the deadline, especially when its goroutine is delayed under load. Claim D therefore does not justify the operator-facing diagnosis.
result.catch: §3.3's assertion that a genuine refusal can only be misclassified within a few milliseconds of the deadline is unverified and has no scheduling bound behind it. T4 tests timestamp classification, not causal attribution. The same unsupported diagnosis becomes the proposed follow-on retry trigger.
result.proposed_fix: Either propagate explicit per-arm failure causes and set out_of_time only when every failed arm is attributable to startup-deadline exhaustion, or retain the timestamp rule but describe only that observation. For the latter, replace the diagnostic with: 'Every failed arm was recorded at or after the startup deadline; startup timeout may have contributed. Review the failure reasons and retry startup if appropriate.' Remove 'host load' and 'nothing to fix in the profile,' revise Claim D, and add a deterministic test where a genuine refusal is recorded after the deadline without being diagnosed as a load-caused failure.
